title: The Mahabharata

explain.say: The Mahabharata is India's great epic about one royal family, the Kurus, split into two sides: the five Pandava brothers and their hundred cousins, the Kauravas. In its longest form it has about 100,000 couplets, making it one of the longest poems ever composed.
The Pandavas are Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva, sons of King Pandu. Their cousins, led by Duryodhana, are the sons of the blind king Dhritarashtra.

items: Elders: Bhishma and the teacher Drona

draw.text: Draupadi is the wife of the five Pandavas; Karna fights for the Kauravas

explain.say: Duryodhana wins the Pandavas' kingdom in a rigged game of dice, and the brothers spend 13 years in exile. When they return and are refused even five villages, the quarrel turns into war.

draw.text: 12 years in the forest, then 1 year in disguise

explain.say: The war is fought for 18 days on the field of Kurukshetra, near modern Delhi. Just before it begins, Krishna speaks the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna, and at the end the Pandavas win, at a terrible cost.

draw.label: Kurukshetra, where the epic's war is set

explain.say: The epic is arranged in 18 books, called parvas, and holds many stories within the main story, as well as teachings on dharma, duty, justice and how to live.

faq.a: The Pandavas are the five sons of King Pandu: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva. They are the heroes of the Mahabharata and fight their cousins the Kauravas at Kurukshetra.
asks: Name the five Pandavas
Who were the Pandava brothers?
How many Pandavas were there?

faq.a: The Kauravas are the hundred sons of the blind king Dhritarashtra and Queen Gandhari, led by the eldest, Duryodhana. They are the Pandavas' cousins and their rivals for the throne of Hastinapura.
asks: Who was Duryodhana?
How many Kauravas were there?
Who are the 100 brothers in the Mahabharata?

faq.a: In its longest form the Mahabharata has about 100,000 couplets, called shlokas, in 18 books. That makes it one of the longest poems in the world, many times longer than the Iliad and Odyssey together.
asks: How many verses are in the Mahabharata?
Is the Mahabharata the longest poem?
How many shlokas does the Mahabharata have?

faq.a: Tradition says the sage Vyasa composed the Mahabharata, and the god Ganesha wrote it down as Vyasa recited it. Many scholars think it was put together by many poets over centuries.
asks: Who is the author of the Mahabharata?
Did Vyasa write the Mahabharata?
Who wrote down the Mahabharata?

faq.q: Why did the Kurukshetra war happen?
faq.a: The Kauravas took the Pandavas' kingdom through a rigged game of dice and sent them into exile for 13 years. When the Pandavas came back, Duryodhana would not return their land, not even five villages, and peace talks led by Krishna failed.
asks: What caused the Mahabharata war?
Why did the Pandavas and Kauravas fight?
What started the war in the Mahabharata?

faq.q: How long did the Kurukshetra war last?
faq.a: The war lasted 18 days. Eighteen appears again and again: there are 18 books, 18 armies, and 18 chapters in the Bhagavad Gita.
asks: How many days was the Mahabharata war?
Why is 18 important in the Mahabharata?
How long was the war at Kurukshetra?

faq.q: How many parvas are in the Mahabharata?
faq.a: The Mahabharata has 18 parvas, or books, from the Adi Parva about the family's beginnings to the Svargarohana Parva, the ascent to heaven. A supplement, the Harivamsha, tells more about Krishna's life.
asks: How many books does the Mahabharata have?
What are the parvas of the Mahabharata?
What is a parva?

faq.q: What is the game of dice in the Mahabharata?
faq.a: Yudhishthira plays dice against Shakuni, the Kauravas' uncle, who cheats. Yudhishthira gambles away his kingdom, his brothers and even Draupadi, and the Pandavas must go into exile.
asks: What happened in the dice game?
How did the Pandavas lose their kingdom?
Who is Shakuni?

faq.a: Draupadi is the princess of Panchala who becomes the wife of all five Pandavas. Her humiliation after the dice game, when Duryodhana's brother tries to disrobe her in court, is a turning point that leads to the war.
asks: Who was Draupadi in the Mahabharata?
Why is Draupadi important?
What happened to Draupadi?

faq.a: Karna is a great warrior, secretly the eldest son of Kunti and so the Pandavas' half brother, though he does not know it until late. Loyal to his friend Duryodhana, he fights on the Kaurava side and is one of the epic's most tragic figures.
asks: Who was Karna?
Was Karna a Pandava?
Why did Karna fight for the Kauravas?

faq.a: Bhishma is the great uncle of both sides, famous for his vow never to marry or claim the throne. He leads the Kaurava army at first, though he loves the Pandavas too, and the Gita is told in the book named after him.
asks: Who was Bhishma?
What was Bhishma's vow?
Why did Bhishma fight for the Kauravas?

faq.q: How is the Bhagavad Gita connected to the Mahabharata?
faq.a: The Gita is a part of the Mahabharata, in the Bhishma Parva. Just before the battle, Arjuna loses heart, and Krishna, his charioteer, teaches him in the 700 verses of the Gita.
asks: Is the Gita in the Mahabharata?
Where does the Gita come in the Mahabharata?
What is the Gita's place in the epic?

faq.a: The Mahabharata explores dharma, what is right, through hard choices where good people make mistakes. It shows the cost of greed, pride and war, and a saying about it claims that what is in it may be found elsewhere, but what is not in it is found nowhere.
asks: What is the moral of the Mahabharata?
What lessons does the Mahabharata teach?
Why is the Mahabharata important?

faq.a: Many historians think the Mahabharata grew over many centuries, roughly between 400 BCE and 400 CE. Hindu tradition places the war much earlier, at the start of the present age, the Kali Yuga, traditionally dated to about 3100 BCE.
asks: How old is the Mahabharata?
When did the Mahabharata happen?
When was the Mahabharata composed?

facts: The Mahabharata has about 100,000 couplets (shlokas) in its longest form, arranged in 18 books called parvas.
The Kurukshetra war in the Mahabharata lasts 18 days.
The five Pandavas are Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva.
Tradition attributes the Mahabharata to the sage Vyasa, with Ganesha as its scribe.
A critical edition of the Mahabharata was prepared at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in Pune between 1919 and 1966.

quiz.say: In the Mahabharata, even heroes like Yudhishthira make serious mistakes, such as gambling away his kingdom. Why might the epic show its heroes this way?
quiz.show: Why does the epic show heroes making mistakes?

options.show: To explore how hard it is to do right
options.say: To explore how hard it can be to know and do what is right
Because the poet disliked the heroes

quiz.why: The Mahabharata is famous for showing dharma as subtle and difficult. Its flawed heroes let readers think about real moral choices.

wrong.1: The epic honours the Pandavas; their flaws make them human, not hated.
wrong.2: The Mahabharata is one of the longest poems ever; brevity was not its aim.
